title: Patient Preparation and Artifact Recognition

sections.learningObjectives:
- Prepare the patient for an ECG, including skin preparation, removal of interfering jewelry and metal, proper positioning, and instructions to lie still and breathe normally.
- Recognize common ECG artifact (muscle tremor, baseline wander, electrical interference, motion) and distinguish it from a good-quality, artifact-free tracing.
- Describe correct electrode handling and contact so that tracings are clean and complete without exceeding the assistant's scope.
- Avoid interpreting ECG results and consistently escalate patient concerns, abnormal findings, persistent artifact, and equipment problems to licensed staff or the provider per office policy.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Wiping the skin first is like cleaning a sticker spot so a sticker stays stuck; a clean spot makes the electrode stay put and pick up the signal.

### Question 2

Jewelry is like a little metal fence that can confuse the machine, so we ask people to take it off, just like taking off a watch before washing hands.

### Question 3

Lying flat and relaxed is like holding a camera very still to take a clear photo; being still and flat gives the machine a clear picture of the heart.

### Question 4

Moving during an ECG is like shaking a camera while taking a picture; the picture (tracing) comes out blurry and hard to read.

### Question 5

During the ECG, we ask people to act like they are taking a calm nap: breathe normally, stay loose, and don't move or chat.

### Question 6

Checking who a person is first is like writing the right name on a school folder before putting papers inside, so nothing gets mixed up.

### Question 7

The ECG is like a microphone for the heart's tiny electrical whispers; it writes them down as wavy lines on paper.

### Question 8

Artifact is like static on a radio that makes the song hard to hear; it is extra noise, not the real music (heartbeat).

### Question 9

Lotion is like a slippery layer that stops a sticker from sticking, so we clean the spot first, the way you dry a wet counter before putting a sticker on it.

### Question 10

Hair is like a fuzzy carpet between the sticker and the skin; if it is too thick, the sticker cannot stick, so we follow the office rules to fix it.

### Question 11

Shivering is like jiggling the table while someone draws; if we warm the person up first, the jiggling stops and the drawing comes out clean.

### Question 12

A wandering baseline is like a wavy, shaky line instead of a flat one, usually because a sticker is loose or the person is wiggling.

### Question 13

This fuzzy interference is like a buzzing hum picked up when a speaker is too close to a phone; moving the phone away stops the buzz.

### Question 14

When muscles shake, they make the line look like a scribble, the same way your hand scribbles if you are shivering while coloring.

### Question 15

A good tracing is like a neat, steady line you can read easily, with no scribbles or fuzz, like neat handwriting.

### Question 16

Talking during an ECG is like moving while getting your picture taken; asking the person to sit still and quiet makes the picture clear.

### Question 17

If someone's heart hurts during the test, that is like a fire alarm going off; you stop and call the grown-up in charge (the provider) right away.

### Question 18

The assistant is like the person who delivers the mail, not the one who reads it; they hand the tracing to the provider and let them figure out what it means.

### Question 19

A loose electrode is like a sticker peeling off; you press it back on (or use a fresh one) and start the picture over.

### Question 20

The assistant is like a photographer who takes a clear picture; the provider is the one who decides what the picture shows and what to do about it.

### Question 21

Privacy during an ECG is like closing the curtain when someone changes clothes; you only uncover the part you need to work on.

### Question 22

Wiping with alcohol is like cleaning a dusty window before putting up a suction cup, so it sticks and works properly.

### Question 23

Artifact happens when two troublemakers team up, like a slippery sticker and a wiggly person; both together make a messy line.

### Question 24

The stickers go on the chest and on the arms and legs, like placing little microphones around the body to hear the heart from many spots.

### Question 25

If lying flat hurts, we help the person get comfortable, like fluffing pillows, and then tell the provider what happened.

### Question 26

Being warm and comfy is like sitting still and calm for a photo; a relaxed body makes a neat, steady line.

### Question 27

The assistant is not the one who reads the test, so they say, 'The provider will explain it,' like a librarian pointing to the expert who knows the answer.

### Question 28

First, we tell the person what we are going to do, like explaining the rules of a game before it starts, so they feel calm and know what to expect.

### Question 29

A flat line usually just means a cord came unplugged, like a TV showing nothing because the cable is loose, so we check the plugs first.

### Question 30

When someone breathes very deeply, their chest moves like gentle waves, and that makes the line rock slowly up and down.

### Question 31

Glasses are like a hat, they do not touch the machine's stickers; metal jewelry near the stickers is what we take off.

### Question 32

Very dry skin is like a cracked, dusty surface where a sticker won't grip; we follow the office's rules to make it ready, and ask if we are not sure.

### Question 33

If the picture came out blurry, you find out why, fix it, and take it again; if it still won't come out, you tell the person in charge.

### Question 34

A 12-lead ECG is like taking 12 photos of the heart from 12 different angles to see it from every side.

### Question 35

A phone near the ECG is like a radio too close to a buzzing speaker; moving the phone away stops the buzz.

### Question 36

If someone suddenly looks very sick during the test, that is like a fire drill; you stop and call for help right away.

### Question 37

Helping someone feel calm is like explaining a scary ride before it starts; knowing what is coming makes them less fidgety.

### Question 38

The ECG is like a report card for the heart's electric beat, showing whether the beats are coming in a steady, healthy rhythm.

### Question 39

Artifact looks like messy scribbles that only happen when the person wiggles, while a clean tracing looks neat and steady.

### Question 40

If one photo out of twelve is blurry but the rest are clear, the blurry one has a smudge; you clean that one lens, not throw out all the photos.

### Question 41

Finishing an ECG is like finishing a school assignment; you write your name on it and hand it to the teacher (provider), not leave it on the desk.

### Question 42

Clammy skin is like a wet window that stickers won't stick to; drying it helps the stickers grip.

### Question 43

When someone is scared of the test, we talk to them kindly and answer questions, like explaining a loud fire drill so it is not so scary.

### Question 44

A hearing aid is like glasses for the ears; we leave it on so the person can hear us explain the test.

### Question 45

The gel is like the glue that helps a microphone touch the speaker better so the sound comes through clearly.

### Question 46

If someone wants to leave before their test, that is like leaving before finishing a class project; we check with the teacher (provider) before they go.

### Question 47

Metal jewelry is like a noisy toy near a quiet recorder; we move it away so it does not mess up the recording.

### Question 48

The lead wires are like phone cords that carry the heart's message from the stickers to the machine that writes it down.

### Question 49

Coughing is like a little jump that makes the pen skip; each cough makes a tiny blip on the line.

### Question 50

If a patient has a heart device, that is important to write down and tell the provider, like flagging a special note on a form for the teacher.

### Question 51

A dried electrode is like a dried-out glue stick; you get a fresh one so it works properly.

### Question 52

Holding your breath is like freezing in a weird pose for a photo; breathing normally keeps everything natural and steady.

### Question 53

A wound dressing is like a bandage you leave alone; we put the sticker somewhere safe and ask the provider where it should go.

### Question 54

The assistant is not the person who reads the test, like a hall monitor who does not grade the test; they pass it to the teacher (provider).

### Question 55

Good skin prep is like a clean, dry spot for a sticker; clean and dry means it sticks and works.

### Question 56

A good tracing is like neat handwriting you can read easily, while a messy one is like scribbles you cannot make out.

### Question 57

If the camera keeps taking blurry photos no matter what we try, we tell the person in charge instead of snapping over and over.

### Question 58

The tracing is like homework that gets handed to the teacher (provider) to grade and act on, not kept by the student.

### Question 59

A frayed cord is like a broken toy with a wire sticking out; you do not play with it, you tell an adult so it gets fixed.

### Question 60

An ECG is like putting cool stickers on the skin; it does not hurt, and taking the stickers off is just a little tug.

### Question 61

Shivering muscles are like a buzzing engine that rattles the line; calm, warm muscles keep the line smooth.

### Question 62

If someone is worried about their heart, we listen and tell the provider, like passing an important note to the teacher instead of answering for them.

### Question 63

Before the test, we check the tools are ready, like making sure the camera has batteries and the lens is clean.

### Question 64

The stickers go right on the skin at the right spots, like placing labels on the correct jars, so the machine hears the heart clearly.

### Question 65

Sweaty skin is like a wet surface a sticker won't stick to; we pat it dry first so the sticker stays.

### Question 66

The patient puts on a gown like changing into a comfy shirt, so the chest is easy to reach for the stickers.

### Question 67

A good baseline is like a flat, calm water line between waves, not a wiggly or fuzzy one.

### Question 68

If someone feels dizzy, we help them stay safe and call the provider, like helping a wobbly friend sit down and calling for help.

### Question 69

To keep the line clean, we do three things: keep the patient warm and still, keep them quiet, and make sure the stickers stick well.

### Question 70

The arm and leg stickers go in their usual spots on bare skin, like placing game pieces in their correct starting squares.

### Question 71

If a person says something feels wrong, we listen and tell the provider, even if the paper looks fine to us, because the provider knows more.

### Question 72

We write the patient's name on the tracing like putting a name on a school paper, so it goes to the right person.

### Question 73

A medicated patch is like a bandage the doctor put on; we leave it alone and put the sticker somewhere else, asking the provider where.

### Question 74

An error message is like a warning light on the car; you stop and tell someone in charge instead of pressing all the buttons.

### Question 75

The resting ECG is like a quick snapshot of the heart's beats, not a long movie; it takes just a few still moments.

### Question 76

A flat baseline is like a clean, blank page with no smudges, so the important writing (heart signal) is easy to read.

### Question 77

If one sticker keeps giving a scribbly line, we write down which one it is and tell the provider, like flagging one blurry photo in a set.

### Question 78

Helping an older patient is like giving a grandparent extra time and a warm blanket so they are comfortable and still.

### Question 79

If the line suddenly jumps when the person shifts, that is the sticker wobbling, not the heart; like a pen skipping when the paper moves.

### Question 80

If someone's chest hurts during the test, we call for help right away and stay with them, like calling for help when someone falls on the playground.

### Question 81

After the stickers come off, we gently wipe away any leftover gel, like cleaning up glue after removing a sticker.

### Question 82

We put the full name on the tracing and make sure it matches the order, like checking the name on a lunchbox before handing it out.

### Question 83

If the picture was blurry, we fix what made it blurry and take it again, just like the provider asked.

### Question 84

The ECG watches the heart's electric beat, like a metronome checking that the beats come in a steady, correct pattern.

### Question 85

A calm patient is like a still, quiet model for a photo; being relaxed makes the picture of the heart come out clean.
